Definitions | التعريفات
arena | ساحة/مضمار/ميدان | a place or situation where a particular activity happens
authentic | أصلي /حقيقي | real and genuine, not false or copied
cognitive | معرفي /إدراكي | relating to mental processes such as thinking, understanding, and learning
engagement | مشاركة / التزام | the act of being involved or interested in an activity
flexibility | مرونة | the ability to change or adapt easily to new situations
rehearsal | بروفة/تدريب | a practice session for a performance before the real event

◆ FOCUS on Vocabulary
لاحظ الفرق بين الكلمات التالية:
rehearsal تدريب/بروفة (تحضير لعرض أو حدث محدد)
- The actors gathered for their final rehearsal before opening night.
- The fire drill was a useful rehearsal for students in an emergency.
training تدريب (اكتساب مهارة جديدة أو تحسين المهارة العامة)
- The swimmer followed a strict training program to prepare for the national championships.
- The ministry is interested in regular training for its teachers to keep their skills up to date.
(1) practice ممارسة/تدريب (تكرار فعل لتحسين المهارة)
Daily piano practice transformed her from a beginner into a confident performer.
authentic أصلي /حقيقي (مطابق للأصل، وليس مقلدا)
- Experts confirmed that the ancient manuscript مخطوطة was authentic.
- The restaurant is known for serving authentic Egyptian food.
genuine صادق/حقيقي /خالص (دون تظوير أو زياء)
- Her smile was so genuine that nobody doubted she was happy.
- She expressed genuine concern for her friend's well-being.
(2) true حق/صحيح /حقيقي (مطابق للواقع أو الحقيقة)
- She proved herself a true friend by staying by my side.
- The story was inspired by true events that took place decades ago.
rank رتبة (عسكرية /اجتماعية)
- My brother was promoted to the rank of captain.
- This hotel was used only by people of high rank.
(3) grade تقديرشهادة /امتحان/ صف دراسي
- He got a grade A in his university degree.
- My brother is in grade six.

B Grammar Focus
Gerund or Infinitive
1 نستخدم (v + ing) بعد to عندما تكون جزءاً من تعبيرات الأتي:
look forward to | يتطلع إلى
confess to | يعترف ب
object to | يعترض على
take to | يعتاد على
(be) (get) used to | يعتاد على
(be/get) accustomed to | يعتاد على
in addition to | بالإضافة إلى
lead to | يؤدي إلى
with a view to | بهدف
when it comes to | عندما يتعلق الأمر بـ
devote to | يكرس الجهود ل
dedicate oneself to | يكرس الجهود ل

addicted to | مدمن على
Examples
The company is close to signing the contract.
When it comes to cooking, she is an expert.
He admitted to cheating on the test.
2 نستخدم (v + ing) بعد العبارات الأتية:
(be) busy | مشغول في

It's (not) worth | يستحق
can't help | لا يستطيع منع

It's no use | لا فائدة من

have trouble | لدية متاعب
what's the use of | ما فائدة
there is no point in | لا جدوى من الجدال
as well as | بالإضافة إلى
don't mind | لا مانع
Examples
I have difficulty understanding math.
She is busy preparing for the exam.
There is no point in arguing.

3 أفعال يأتي بعدها to + infinitive أو verb + ing بدون تغيير في المعنى.
hate | يكره | like | يحب | love | يحب
prefer | يفضل | start | يبدأ | continue | يستمر
intend | ينوى | begin | يبدأ | bother | يُزعج / يضايق
I intend to study medicine/intend studying medicine after finishing school.
The company began to cut costs/began cutting costs due to the recession.
الـظ إذا كان الفعل في صيغة المضارع المستمر يأتي بعده to + infinitive
Take your umbrella; it's starting to rain. (Not: raining)
4 أفعال يأتي بعدها to + infinitive أو verb + ing وهناك تغيير في المعنى:
stop
stop + (verb + ing) | يتوقف عن فعل شيء لفترة أو يتلق عن الشيء تماما.
stop + (to + infinitive) | يتوقف عن شيء ليفعل شيئاً آخر (هدف) وغالباً عندما يكون ماشياً.
He stopped taking sugar in his tea because he is on a strict diet.
On his way to the office, he stopped to take cash from the ATM.
remember
remember + (verb + ing) | يتذكر أنه فعل شيئاً تم الحدوث أوْلًم ثم تذكّر بعده ذلك.
remember + (to + infinitive) | يتذكر أن يفعل شيئاً يتذكر أوْلًم ثم يفعل الشيء بعده ذلك.
I remember locking the safe before leaving. I can clearly picture doing it.
Please remember to lock the safe before you leave tonight.

forget
forget + (verb + ing) | تم حدوث الشيء أوْلًم ثم نسيه أو لم ينتبه بعده ذلك.
forget + (to + infinitive) | نسي أن يفعل الشيء أصلاً فهُمّدأو ينسى ليفعله بعده ذلك.
She will never forget meeting the President; it was an unforgettable day.
She forgot to meet the client at the airport, so he took a taxi.
regret
regret + (verb + ing) | فعل شيئاً ثم ندم بعده ذلك.
regret + (to + infinitive) | يأسف أن يقول شيئاً أو يفعل شيئاً محطراً لذلك.
I regret selling my old car; the new one breaks down constantly.
We regret to inform you that your application has been rejected.
try
try + (verb + ing) | حاول أن يفعل شيئاً ونجح فيه – يحاول تجريب شيء ويري نتيجته.
try + (to + infinitive) | يحاول أن يفعل شيئاً بكل الجهده.
If you have a headache, try drinking more water before taking medicine.
The doctor tried to save the patient, but the injury was fatal.

◆ Topic overview | نظرة عامة على الموضوع
What it means to move, compete, and belong
Sport is one of the most beneficial leisure activities for young people. It improves not only physical health but also mental well-being. However, many teenagers today are becoming less active due to screens and academic pressure. In this lesson, we will discover why moving more can change your life.

Inquiry Question: | سؤال بحثي
What are the physical, mental, and social benefits of sport for young people?
ما الفوائد الجسدية والعقلية والاجتماعية التي تعود على الشباب من ممارسة الرياضة؟

Suggested answer:
Sport helps young people grow by providing key benefits:
Physical: Strengthening muscles and bones, boosting heart health, and maintaining fitness.
Mental: Reducing stress, building discipline, and increasing self-confidence.
Social: Teaching teamwork, improving communication, and fostering strong friendships.

Scan & listen

◆ Listening Text
The Benefits of Sports Pyramid: From Foundation to Peak
"Moving More: Why Sport Matters for Young People"
The World Health Organization recommends that young people aged 5-17 should get at least sixty minutes of medium to hard physical activity every day. Yet across the world—and increasingly in Egypt—many teenagers fall far short of this target. A 2024 survey(1) conducted by the Egyptian Ministry of Youth and Sports found that fewer than one in three secondary school students met the recommended weekly activity levels. The rise of inactive lifestyles, driven by screen time and intense academic pressure, has created what some experts call a "movement crisis(2) " among the young.
The benefits of regular sport extend well beyond physical fitness(3). Heart health, stronger bones, and healthy weight management are the most obvious advantages, but the psychological and social gains may be even more significant. Psychologists have found that young people who participate(4) in team sports show higher levels of self-esteem, better emotional regulation, and greater social competence(5) than their non-sporting peers. Sport teaches young people how to lose gracefully(6), how to support teammates in difficult moments, and how to persevere(7) through difficulty, all life skills of immeasurable value that transfer directly into academic and professional contexts.
Access to sport is not the same for everyone. Some young people have easy access to sports facilities(8), safe places, and support from their families or schools. However, others may not have these opportunities because of cost, location, or lack of resources(9). This makes it harder for them to take part in physical activity. It is important to find ways to give all young people a fair chance to enjoy sport.
The evidence on what makes young people stay active throughout their lives is remarkably consistent(10): enjoyment is the strongest predictor of long term participation. When young people are forced into competitive sport they dislike, or when failure is treated harshly, they disengage(11). Young people who find sports they genuinely love—whether competitive or enjoyable, individual or team-based—are far more likely to remain active into adulthood(12). The challenge for educators and families is therefore to expand the range of sporting options available, so that every student can find their own movement and carry it with them through life.

Definitions | التعريفات
cardiovascular | قلبي / وعائى | relating to the heart and blood vessels/tubes through which blood flows around your body
competence | كفاءة/إتقان | the ability to do something well
facilities | مرافق /تجهيزات | a place or building used for a particular activity or industry, or for providing a certain type of service
gracefully | برشاقة /بأنسلوب متزن | moving in a smooth and attractive way, or having an attractive shape or form/in a polite and pleasant way
persevere | يثابر /يواصل بإصرار | to continue trying to do something in a very determined way in spite of difficulties
survey | استبيان /مسبح | a set of questions that you ask a large number of people in order to find out about their opinions or behavior

transmit

3 target

goal

- يهدف إلى وبأتى بعدها (at – to – for)

21. Karim practiced every day and got better at playing the guitar. His teacher said he showed great competence. What does "competence" mean here?
a) The desire to be liked by everyone at work.
b) The tendency to rely on others for every decision.
c) The ability to do something well.
d) The habit of avoiding difficult tasks.
22. Though the math problem was very hard, Layla did not give up. She kept trying until she solved it. Her teacher said she showed great power as she continued to persevere. What does "persevere" mean here?
a) To keep trying, even when something is difficult.
b) To give up quickly when something is hard.
c) To ask someone else to do the work for you.
d) To ignore a problem completely.
23. Before opening a new shop, Omar wanted to know what people liked. He gave 100 people a list of questions to answer. This is called a survey. What does "survey" mean here?
a) A type of an academic test to qualify students to do a certain job.
b) A big building where people shop for different kinds of goods.
c) A scientific study on chemistry, physics, or math.
d) A set of questions used to learn what many people think.
24. After weeks of intense preparation, the team were finally ready for the match. The opposite of the adjective "intense" is "...................".
a) powerful | b) relieved | c) gentle | d) strong
25. Working twelve-hour shifts every day really tests a nurse's physical and mental endurance. The noun "endurance" can be replaced by "..................".
a) weakness | b) stamina | c) laziness | d) affection

Sport plays an important role in the lives of many young people. Regular exercise helps improve (1).................... (fit) and keeps the body healthy. Many schools provide physical sports (2).................... (facility) where students can train and take part in different activities. Some students enjoy (3).................... (compete) sports because they like the challenge of competing against others. To continue participating, young people need strong (4).................... (motivate) and encouragement from their families and teachers.

B Grammar Focus
1 Gerund (verb + ing)
1 نستخدم (verb + ing) كاسم أول الكلام محل الفاعل ويعامل معاملة المفرد أي يكون الفعل بعده:
"is/was/has/does/v-s/es/ies"
Getting up early strengthens your body and makes you active.
Reading books and stories is interesting.
2 نستخدم (verb + ing) بعد حروف الجر ما عدا (to) التي تأتي بعدها المصدر:
He left the shop without paying, so he was accused of stealing.
3 نستخدم gerund (verb + ing) كاسم فاعل (present participle) ولا يأتي فعل آخر في الجملة الأولى التي تسبق الفاصلة (,).
Feeling tired, I went back home to have some rest.
Looking out of the window, I saw a strange bird.
لاحظ عند النفي نضع not قبل (v + ing).
ويمكن أن يأتي present participle وسط الجملة بدلًا من and مثل:
Not wanting to get low marks, I studied hard day and night.
I switched on the TV expecting to watch the match, but it was encrypted.
4 نستخدم gerund (verb + ing) بعد أدوات الربط الزمنية الآتية إذا ألم يأتي فعل بعدها مع ملاحظة أن الفعل الثاني هو نفس الفعل المضروف.
After | After finishing my homework, I helped my brother.
Before | Before helping my brother, I had finished my homework.
While | While driving through the city center, I ran out of petrol.
When | When arriving home, Ali greets everyone in the flat.
since | Ali has been taking a new route home since seeing a violent dog there.
5 يمكن أن يأتي gerund (verb + ing) بعد صفة ملكية أو اسم في حالة الملكية.
I appreciate your helping me.
Do you mind my opening the window?
2 to + inf.
1 الاستخدام الأساسي لـ to بمعنى لكي وهى تعبر عن الهدف والغرض:
to / in order to / so as to
He works hard to support his family.
He works hard in order to support his family.
He works hard so as to support his family.

2 وفي النفي to not بمعنى لكي لا / نلا:
He left early in order not to miss the train.
He left early so as not to miss the train.

◆ Important Notes
1 نستخدم to/so that للهدف إذا كان الفاعل واحداً أما إذا اختلف الفاعل نستخدم فقط so that.
so that | in order that | in the hope that | لكي | جملة كاملة subject + modal verb + inf. | جملة كاملة Subject + verb + ...
I study hard so that my father will be happy.
I exercise every day so that my children can learn healthy habits.
يجب مراعاة أنه لو كان الفعل ماضياً قبل so that تكون الجملة ماضيّاً بعدها.
I studied hard so that I could get high marks.
2 نستخدم too + adjective + to بمعنى جدا لدرجة أنه لا (دائما الجملة تعطي معنى النفي والصفة سلبية للموقف التي فيه)
He's too shy to meet the strangers. هو خجول لدرجة أنه لا يُقابل الغرباء.
Ali is too short to hang the picture. على قصير لدرجة أنه لا يستطيع أن يعلق الصورة.
من الممكن أن يكون على ليس قصيراً في الحقيقة ولكن موضوع تعليق الصورة هو المرتفع.
The question is too difficult for me to answer.
في الجملة استخدمنا for ثم المفصول للتخصيص ولو حذفناها لكان السؤال لايمكن حله من أي شخص.
الجملة بعد to تكون في المعلومات دائما ولا يصح أن نقول to be answered حتى مع حذف for.
The box is too heavy to carry.
The car is too expensive to buy.
لاحظ أن busy يأتي بعدها gerund وإذا سبقتها too فيبعدها يكون اما to + inf. أو gerund حسب المعنى.
He's too busy attending the meetings. مشغول جداً بحضور الاجتماعات.
He's too busy to attend the meetings. مشغول بأنشئاء تمنعه من حضور الاجتماعات.
3 نستخدم adjective + enough بمعنى بدرجة كافية (الصفة دائما إيجابية للموقف الذي نحن فيه).
My brother is clever enough to pass the test.
The question is easy enough to answer.
ويمكن نفي الفعل الذي قبل enough للتعبير عن عدم الكفاية.
The car isn't cheap enough to buy.
في الجملة السابقة حذفت for والشخص الذي بعدها لأنه ليس من المعقول أن السيارة مرتفعة الثمن على كل الناس.
4 الأفعال advise/permit/allow/forbid يأتي بعدها verb + ing إذا لم يأتي بعدهم مفعول.
My teacher advised taking a course during the summer vacation.
They don't allow smoking inside the office.

5 نستخدم to+ inf :
(1) بعد الأفعال الآتية للتعبير عن الرغبة في وقت معين:
would like / would love / would prefer
I would like to see the manager.
(ب) بعد الصفات الدالة على المشاعر والعواطف happy, glad, sorry, surprised, etc.
She was sorry to miss the conference.
(جـ) بعد only للتعبير عن نتيجة غير مرغوبية.
He came only to meet his friend Ahmed.
(د) بعد the first/second, etc. / next /last / best, etc.
He was the first to come to the party.
(هـ) عوضا عن الجملة التي تحتوي على should.
My uncle is the person whom you should see. He's the person to see.
3 The infinitive without (to) with the following:
1 نستخدم المصدر بدون (to) بعد التعبيرات والأفعال الآتية:
had better | ينفعي | would rather | من الأفضل | let | يسمح
make | يعمل | help (inf or to + inf) | يساعد | know | يعرف
The thieves made the man empty his pocket.
Sarah'd better take the umbrella with her in case it rains.
إذا جاء فاعل بعد (would rather ('d نستخدم الماضي البسيط إذا كانت الجملة تعبرعن المضارع والماضي التام إذا كانت الجملة تعبرعن الماضي.
I'd rather Ali went to bed early.
I'd rather Ali had gone to bed early yesterday.
2 نستخدم المصدر infinitive فقط أيضاً بعد الآتي:
- بعد modal verbs مثل can/will/must ... etc.
You can leave now if you want.
- بعد الأفعالين suggest/ recommend إذا كان بعدها فاعل ( أي فاعل)
He suggested that she help the children with their homework.
4 The infinitive or the gerund
لاحظ شكل الفعل بعد الأفعال التالية:
go on
go on +(verb + ing) | يستمر فى عمل شىء.
go on + (to + infinitive) | يستمر فى عمل شىء بعد الانتهاء من شىء آخر.
She went on talking for hours.
After finishing the report, she went on to type some letters.
mean
mean + (verb + ing) | يشمل/يتضمن
mean + (to + infinitive) | ينوى /يهدف إلى
Finding a job means attending many interviews.
He means to find a job abroad.

need
need + (verb + ing) | يُأتَى قِبَلَها الفاعل غير عاقل (مبني للمجهول في المعنى) أو يُوقع عليه الفعل ومعناها يريد شيء أن يُفعل
need + (to + infinitive) | يجب أن
My shoes are quite dull. They need polishing. (to be polished)
My shoes are quite dull. I need to polish them.
see/hear/listen to/watch
see/hear/listen to/watch + (verb + ing) | يسمع أوبى جزءًا من الحدث.
see/hear/listen to/watch + (infinitive) | يسمع أوبى الحدث كله.
I watched my father painting the living room. | رأيت والدي يدفع الحجرة (جزءًا من الحدث).
I watched my father paint the living room. | رأيت والدي يدفع الحجرة من البداية إلى النهاية.
الــظ | إذا جاءت could/ can قبل see/hear فبأتي بعدها verb + ing .
I could see him painting the house.

◆ Topic overview | نظرة عامة على الموضوع
What it means to find meaning through unexpected outdoor experiences
When we face unexpected situations outdoors, we often learn lessons that contribute to our personal experience and mental growth. For instance, being caught in a sudden rainstorm or navigating a difficult trail forces us to be fully present in the moment. This shift in focus moves us away from daily stressors and towards the immediate environment. Ultimately, overcoming these obstacles provides a sense of excitement and achievement that makes the experience truly meaningful.
Inquiry Question: سؤال بحثي
What does genuine leisure require: comfort, challenge, or something else?
ما الذى يتطلبه الترفيه الحقيقي: الراحة، أو التحدي، أوأى شيء آخر؟
Suggested answer:
Genuine leisure requires a balance of active challenge and personal growth rather than mere comfort.

◆ Reading Text
اقرأ القطعة ثم أجب عن الأسئلة للتدريب على اسئلة قطعة الفهم.
Not Exactly a Relaxing Day
Literary Extract: A personal narrative set along the Nile.
1. Read the extract carefully. As you read, note the narrator's changing mood and tone and underline words or phrases that show how his feelings shift.
My idea of leisure was simple: stay at home, watch a series, and do absolutely nothing. I used to believe that the best way to spend a free day was in complete stillness—a full afternoon on the sofa, curtains half-closed against the afternoon sun, a cold glass of water on the table beside me. However, my friend insisted(1) that I join him on a cycling trip along the Nile. "It will be relaxing," he said. "You'll feel amazing afterwards." I believed him.
صبر (1) | يثاق (2)
2. Read the next section. Give a sentence that summarizes the narrator's initial experience.
We started early in the morning, before the city had fully woken up. The air was still cool, the road was quiet, and the Nile shimmered(2) softly beside us. For the first hour, everything felt exactly as promised. We cycled slowly, enjoying the view of the river, the sound of the water, and the occasional call of birds settling on the bank. I even began to think that outdoor activities were not as exhausting as I had always imagined and that my friend had been right all along.

3. As you read the following sections, underline any word or phrase that shows the narrator's attitude changing.
Then, things changed. The road became longer and less shaded. The sun, which had been gentle and golden at dawn, grew stronger and more direct as the morning wore on(5). My energy began to disappear. My friend, who clearly كافح الاستمرار(6) | يمربالتدريج(5) ضغطة دواسة(7) شعوراً بإنجاز(8)
had considerably more experience, continued cycling as if nothing had happened as if the heat were simply decoration and the distance were a minor detail. Meanwhile, I struggled to keep up(6). My legs ached. My breathing was uneven. At one point, I seriously considered giving up and calling a taxi home.
But something stopped me. Perhaps it was pride, the unwillingness to admit defeat in front of someone who was making it look so effortless. Or perhaps it was something less comfortable to admit: that I was genuinely curious whether I could finish. Step by step, I kept going. We took short breaks in the shade, drank water, laughed at my complaints, and continued moving forward. Each time I thought about stopping. I took one more pedal stroke(7) instead. When we finally stopped, I realized we had cycled much farther than I had expected. I was exhausted in a way I had never quite experienced before: a deep, physical tiredness that sat in my legs and shoulders like warm sand. But I was also, strangely, satisfied. Sitting beside the Nile, drinking cold juice, watching the afternoon light change on the water, I felt a sense of achievement(8) that no quiet afternoon at home could ever have given me.
That day changed my understanding of leisure. It is not always about comfort or doing nothing. Sometimes, the best moments come from effort, from pushing past the point where you wanted to stop, and from discovering—with some surprise—that you were more capable than you thought.
Source
"An original pedagogical narrative set along the Nile, custom-authored by the curriculum development team to structurally scaffold the interaction of three past narrative tenses and model emotional shifts across the passive-to-active leisure spectrum.
JRE (Justify – Reason – Evidence) | مجاب عن نهاية الكتاب.

2. Difficult experiences can lead to greater satisfaction. To what extent do you agree? Give evidence from the text. SB

Definitions | التعريفات
insisted | أصر | demanded firmly and repeatedly that someone do something
pedal stroke | ضغطة دواسة | a single push of the pedal when cycling
sense of achievement | شعورا بالإنجاز | a strong, proud feeling gained from completing something difficult
shimmer | يتألق | to shine with a soft, slightly moving light
struggled to keep up | كافح للاستمرار | advanced slowly and continuously, with great difficulty
wore on | يمري بالتدريج | passed gradually (used of time)

الاحظ الفرق بين الكلمات التالية:
1 pain | ألم (شعوربه وغالبا يكون بشكل مفاجئ) | - A broken leg causes a lot of pain. - He felt a sharp pain in his chest.
ache | ألم (مستمر غالبا ليس شديدا وممكن أن تستخدم في الأسماء المركبة) | - I felt an ache in my back after wandering all day. - Driving gives me a headache. - I've got a stomachache.

2 realize | ١- يدرك (يعرف أو يفهم شيئا) ٢- يحقق (شيئا كان يتمناه). | - Do you realize you're an hour late? - She never realized her ambition of winning an Olympic gold medal.
recognize | ١- يتعرف على (يعرف شخصا أو شيئا لرؤيته أو سماعه أو الصوربه من قبل) ٢- يقبل ويعرف أهمية شيئ. | - I didn't recognize you in your uniform. - The new doctor tried to get his work recognized by the medical profession.
3 experience | ١- خبرة (في العمل مثلا) ويعتبر اسما غير معدود. ٢- تجربة حياتية ويعتبر اسما معدودا. ٣- يمر بتجربة (في الحياة/العمل). | - The best way to learn is by experience. - The young woman had some frightening experiences when she was kidnapped by a gang. - The day I failed the test was one of the worst days I've ever experienced.
experiment | ١- تجربة علمية أو معملية. ٢- يقوم بتجربة (لاختبار أو إثبات نظرية أو مفهوم علمي). | - In science classes, students carry out simple laboratory experiments. - I am totally against researchers experimenting on animals.
4 series | تستخدم كلمة (series) بمعان مختلفة ولها نفس الشكل في المفرد والجمع: مجموعة من الكتب أو البرامج التلفزيونية أو الأحداث ذات الصلة. | - My sister enjoys watching a popular series about young detectives.
عدد من الأشياء المتشابهة التي تحدث تباعا. | - A series of heavy storms caused flooding across the region.
مجموعة من الكتب أو المنشورات التعليمية. | - Our school uses a series of English textbooks for different grade levels.
مجموعة من العناصر العلمية أو الرياضية المتتابعة. | - The teacher explained how to find the sum of a number series in math.
سلسلة من التجارب أو الإجراءات. | - The scientists conducted a series of tests before announcing their results.

B Grammar Focus
Summary
أولاً: Gerund (v + ing)
نسـتخدم الفعـل مضـافاً إليه ing في الحالات التالية:
1 بعد أفعال محددة: مثل (avoid, enjoy, suggest, admit, consider, finish, risk).
2 بعد تعبيرات تنتهي بـ (to): مثل (look forward to, object to, (be) used to, in addition to, lead to, confess to) .
3 تعبيرات اصطلاحية: مثل (It's no use, It's no good, can't help, can't stand, feel like, be busy) .
4 كفاعل بداية للجملة (Reading books is interesting).
5 بعد حروف الجر: مثل (without, accused of) .
المجهول منها: يكون باستخدام (being + P.P.) .
ثانياً: (to + inf.)
نسـتخدم المصـدر المسبوق بـ to في الحالات التالية:
1 أفعـال مباشـرة: مـثـل (decide, plan, hope, agree, refuse, manage, seem) .
2 أفعـال يتبعها مفعـول به ثم المصـدر: مـثـل (advise, allow, encourage, persuade, tell) .
3 للتعبير عن الغرض : باستخدام (to, in order to, so as to) .
4 بعد الصفات: مثل (happy to, sorry to) أو صيغ (too + adj + to) و (adj + enough to) .
المجهول منها: يكون باستخدام (to be + P.P.) .
ثالثاً: « المصدر » بدون to (Bare Infinitive)
يأتي الفعل بدون (to) وبدون (ing) بعد:
1 الأفعال الناقصة (can, will, must) .
2 تعبيرات محددة: (had better, would rather, let, make) .
3 بعد (suggest / recommend) في حال وجود فاعل بعدها.
رابعاً: Gerund (v + ing) or (to + inf.)
هناك أفعال تتغير معناها تماًماً حسب ما بعدها:
1 (+ing) : stop يتوقف عن الفعل نهائياً؛ (+ to) stop يتوقف لكي يفعل شيئاً آخر.
2 remember/forget: (+ing) يتذكر/ينسى حدثاً تم بالفعل؛ (remember/forget + to) يتذكر/ينسى أن يقوم بفعل .
3 regret: (+ing) يندم على شى فعله؛ (+ to) regret يأسف لأنه مصطر لقول خبر سيئ.
4 try: (+ing) يجرب ليرى النتيجة؛ (+ to) try يحاول بذل جهد ومشقة.
5 go on: (+ing) يستمر في نفس الفعل؛ (+ to) go on ينتقل لفعل شى جديد..

خامساً: أفعال الحواس (رؤية وسمـاع الحدث)
أفعـال مثـل (see, watch, hear) يأتي بعدها:
1 (+ing) تعني أذنك رأيت أو سمعت جزءاً من الحدث.
2 (Infinitive) تعني أذنك رأيت أو سمعت الحدث من بدايته للنهاية.
سادساً: ملاحظات
1 أفعـال (love, hate, prefer, start, begin) تأخذ الاثنين بدون اختلاف كبير في المعنى .
2 لكن : إذا سبقها (would) مثـل (would like/love) يجب استخدام (to + inf.) فقط..
3 إذا كان فعل (start/begin) نفسه في زمن المستمر, نستخدم بعده (to + inf.) فقط..

القسم C | Section (C): المهارات — Study Skills

1 Opinion Paragraph | فقرة إبداء الرأي

An opinion paragraph clearly states your stance on a topic and persuades the reader to agree using supporting evidence.
توضيح فقرة إبداء الرأي موقفك بوضوح من موضوع ما وتقنع القارئ بالموافقة باستخدام الأدلة الداعمة.

Structure of Opinion Paragraph

Opinion (Claim) | Reason
State your opinion clearly. | Give a reason to support your opinion.
عبّر عن رأيك بوضوح. | قدّم سبباً يدعم رأيك.

Example /Evidence | Conclusion
Add an example or explanation. | Restate your opinion in a different way.
أضف مثالاً أو شرحاً. | أعيد صياغة رأيك بطريقة مختلفة.

2 Model Paragraph

What does it mean to have a balanced leisure life in today's world?

In today's world, having a balanced leisure life means spending free time in different useful and enjoyable ways. People are often busy with school, work, or daily responsibilities, so they need time to relax and have fun. A balanced leisure life includes different types of activities. For example, people can play sports to stay healthy, read books to learn new things, and spend time with family and friends to feel happy and connected. It is also important not to spend all free time on phones, social media, or video games. Trying hobbies such as drawing, music, or gardening can make life more interesting. A good balance between work and leisure helps people feel less stressed and more energetic. In my opinion, everyone should use their free time wisely and enjoy a variety of activities. This can improve their health, happiness, and overall quality of life.

A Diary Entry    مذكرة يومية
Writing a diary entry is simply recording your daily experiences, reflections, and emotions in an honest, personal space.
كتابة مذكراتك اليومية تعنى ببساطة تسجيل تجاربك، وتأملاتك، ومشاعرك اليومية في مساحة شخصية صادقة.
Structure of A Diary Entry
Opening    افتتاح
Date and salutation    التاريخ والتحية
Set the scene: where were you, what had you just done
وصف المكان: أين كنت؟ وماذا كنت تفعل للتو؟
The story    القصة
Recount the main events in order using narrative tenses. Include: the first hour (positive), the turning point (difficulty), the decision to keep going.
أعد سرد الأحداث الرئيسية بالترتيب باستخدام أزمنة السرد. يشمل ذلك: الساعة الأولى (إيجابية)، نقطة التحول (صعوبة)، قرارا للاستمرار.
Turning point    نقطة تحول
Describe the moment you most wanted to stop. What stopped you? Use Past Continuous to show what was happening around you at that moment.
صف اللحظة التي شعرت فيها برغبة شديدة في التوقف. ما الذي منعك؟ استخدم صيغة الماضي المستمر لتوضيح ما كان يحدث حولك في تلك اللحظة.
Reflection    تفكير
How did it feel when you finally stopped? Use a simile or vivid detail to describe your exhaustion and your satisfaction.
كيف كان شعورك عندما توقفت أخيراً؟ استخدم تشبيهاً أو وصفاً دقيقاً لوصف إرهاقك ورضاك.
The ending    النهاية
What did this experience teach you about yourself?
This is the diary's 'message'— make it personal and honest.
ماذا علمتك هذه التجربة عن نفسك؟
هذه هي «رسالة» اليوميات – اجعلها شخصية وصادقة.
Final sentence    الجملة الأخيرة
End with a memorable line that captures your key insight. It can be funny, philosophical, or both.
اختم بعبارات لا تُنسى تُلخص فكرتك الرئيسية. يمكن أن تكون هذه العبارة فكاهية، أو فلسفية، أو كلتيهما.
Model Diary Entry
Dear Diary,
Today was a wonderful day. After several days of dull weather, the sunshine finally returned. The bright sky and warm sun made me feel cheerful from the moment I woke up.
I decided to spend the day outdoors and went for a long bike ride. At first, I felt a little tired, but I kept going and soon began to enjoy the fresh air and the beautiful views around me. The river shimmered in the sunlight, and everything seemed more lively and colorful. By the end of the ride, I felt proud of what I had achieved.
This experience taught me an important lesson about leisure and happiness. I learned that happiness does not always come from expensive things or exciting events. Simple activities, such as cycling and spending time in nature, can make us feel relaxed and satisfied. Leisure is not just a way to pass time; it helps us stay healthy, reduce stress, and enjoy life more.
I am ending this day feeling happy, grateful, and refreshed.

Modern teenagers navigate an environment that is soaked with digital displays. Recent studies indicate that young people spend approximately seven hours a day on personal devices, a figure that excludes academic requirements. This sedentary lifestyle has driven a significant drop in physical activity. Medical experts and worried parents are increasingly alarmed by this digital absorption, as heavy screen habits often interfere with natural sleep cycles, reduce real-world social development, and harm academic performance.
Social media platforms like Instagram and TikTok present a unique challenge to a teenager's self-esteem. Users are constantly exposed to carefully chosen, highly filtered images of their peers' lives. This creates a psychological phenomenon known as the "highlight-reel effect," where teenagers compare their ordinary daily lives to the idealized versions of others. This comparison can cause young people to develop a false sense of their own worth, leading them to withdraw from offline social interactions due to heightened anxiety and a fear of not being good enough.
However, researchers emphasize that the ultimate solution is not total restriction but achieving a healthy balance. Total digital isolation is unrealistic in a modern society where technology is necessary. Instead, teenagers who learn to set clear boundaries—such as establishing screen-free family meals or avoiding devices an hour before sleeping—report feeling far more in control of their habits. Mindful technology use combined with offline activities can significantly enhance their well-being.

2 Read the following passage, then answer the questions:
Spending too much time looking at screens is not good for young people. Today, many teenagers sit for hours playing video games, scrolling through social media, or watching random online videos. This modern lifestyle makes them very active online but extremely lazy in real life. Instead of sitting all day, choosing creative hobbies like painting, drawing, or
(5) playing music is much better for the mind. When teenagers create art, their brains work hard to make something completely new. This active thinking keeps their minds sharp, fresh, and healthy. It gives them a sense of happiness that a computer screen can never provide.
Also, playing regular sports is very important for every teenager. Sports do not just make the human body strong and healthy; they also teach great social lessons that books cannot
(10) explain. In team sports like football, basketball, or volleyball, teenagers learn how to work together as one group, communicate politely with others, and control their anger during difficult moments. They also learn how to lose a game without getting sad and how to help a teammate who feels down or disappointed. These simple but vital life skills help them greatly when they grow up, enter university, and get professional jobs.
(15) However, the most important thing about any hobby or sport is having real fun. If parents or teachers force teenagers to play a sport they do not like, they will get bored and stop playing it very quickly. The best way to solve this problem is to let young people choose what they truly love. When teenagers freely discover their favorite activities, they will continue to stay active, happy, and creative for the rest of their lives.

3 Read the text, then answer the questions:

Nadia used to enjoy taking photos, but recently, posting them on social media had become stressful. Every morning, she checked the accounts of several popular teenagers before getting ready for school. Their clothes always looked fashionable, their rooms seemed perfect, and their weekends were full of exciting activities. Nadia began to feel that her ⑤ own life was ordinary and uninteresting.

One Friday, Nadia and her best friend, Jana, went to a small café after school. They laughed, talked about their week, and shared a piece of chocolate cake. Nadia took several photos, but before posting one, she spent nearly twenty minutes editing it. She changed the light, removed a small mark from her face, and carefully chose a picture that made the café look ⑩ more expensive than it really was. Finally, she posted it with the words, "Perfect afternoon!"

A few minutes later, the photo received many likes. At first, Nadia felt pleased. Then Jana looked at her and smiled. "It was a lovely afternoon," she said, "but it wasn't perfect. We waited thirty minutes for our food, and you almost dropped the cake!" They both laughed. Suddenly, Nadia realized something important. She was doing exactly what other people ⑮ did online—showing only the best part of an experience.

That evening, Nadia looked again at some of the accounts she usually followed. This time, she viewed them differently. Perhaps the people in those perfect photos also had difficult days, worries, and ordinary moments that nobody saw. She understood that comparing her complete life with someone else's selected moments was unfair.

⑳ Over the next few weeks, Nadia changed some of her online habits. She unfollowed accounts that regularly made her feel less confident and followed people who shared realistic stories and positive messages. She also reduced the time she spent checking her phone.

Instead, she joined a school art club and began meeting Jana for walks on weekends. Nadia did not stop using social media. She still enjoyed sharing photos and keeping ㉕ in touch with friends, but she no longer measured a good day by the number of likes she received. She had learned that social media could be enjoyable and useful, but real confidence came from accepting herself and appreciating the life she actually lived.

(5) الوحدة 3 | CONCEPT 3: Identity | UNIT 3: Echoes of the Past
==========================================================================================

◆ Unit Overview:
This unit explores the concept of identity through how memory and history are created, kept, and sometimes debated in Egypt and the wider world. You will study how places hold shared memories, how museums tell historical stories, and how digital platforms are changing the way historical events are recorded and shared. Through four integrated lessons, you will build your language proficiency across the four key skills.

◆ Learning Objectives:
You will be able to:
Reading : Analyze historical narratives and identify the writer's viewpoint.
Listening : Listen to media reports about discoveries and distinguish between stated and unstated information.
Speaking : Present a site analysis, expressing a clear opinion, and recognize an opposing viewpoint.
Writing : Write a discursive paragraph that weighs different perspectives, uses concession clauses, and supports ideas with evidence.
Content Objectives | الأهداف الخاصة بالمحتوى
You will:
- identify how sites of memory preserve collective identity.
- analyze how museums select and present historical narratives.
- evaluate the role of social media in documenting history.
- examine how viral content shapes historical understanding.
- construct structured arguments using the JRE [Justify, Reason, Evidence] framework.
Language Objectives | الأهداف الخاصة بمهارات اللغة الإنجليزية
You will:
- use prepositional phrases of place and time accurately.
- use concession clauses to demonstrate counter-arguments.
- write a discursive paragraph and a personal landmark analysis.
- take part in structured discussions and presentations.

◆ Topic overview | نظرة عامة على الموضوع
Why historical sites still matter
Ancient monuments and historical sites play an important role in preserving the identity and heritage of nations. They reflect the achievements of past civilizations and help people understand their history more deeply. Exploring these landmarks allows visitors to connect with the past, appreciate cultural values, and learn important lessons that continue to influence society and future generations.

Inquiry Question: سؤال بحثي
What makes a place a "site of memory"? How is it different from an ordinary historical building?
ما الذي يجعل مكانًا ما «موقعًا للذاكرة»؟ وكيف يختلف عن مبنى تاريخي عادي؟

Suggested answer:
A "site of memory" is a place that carries deep emotional, symbolic, and cultural meaning for a community or nation.
An ordinary historical building, on the other hand, is old or architecturally significant, and tells you what happened in the past.

◆ Listening Text
Scan & listen
The Stones That Remember: A Walk Through Karnak
When I stood at the entrance to Karnak Temple Complex in Luxor for the first time, I was not struck by its size although it is truly enormous, but by its silence. In the early morning, before the tour groups arrive, the avenue of ram-headed sphinxes(1) stretches southward in near-perfect stillness, each one carved from sandstone that was already ancient when Cleopatra walked beside it. In the space between the columns, with the first light falling at a low angle across the hieroglyphics, it feels as if time has not moved at all.
Karnak is not a single building but a landscape of accumulated(2) memory, built over more than two thousand years from the reign of Senusret in the Middle Kingdom to the Ptolemaic era.
The complex represents the longest continuous building project in human history. Each pharaoh added, changed, or inscribed(3) something, leaving layers of devotion(4) and ambition encoded(5) in stone. The Hypostyle Hall alone contains 134 massive(6) columns, decorated from floor to ceiling. This space was designed not simply to impress but to communicate: it belonged to the gods, and the pharaoh was their representative(7) on earth.
(1) مُتَرَاكِمَة | (2) أَبُو الْهَوْل بِرَأْسِ الْكَبْش
(3) نَقَش/سَجَّل | (4) تَفَانِي
(5) مُشَفَّرَة | (6) ضَخْم
(7) مَمَثَّل
What I find most significant, however, is not what has survived, but the question the site invites us to ask as Egyptians today. Karnak was not built for tourists, it was built for a civilization. Yet as we walk through its vast spaces, we are reminded that history is not only something we observe, but something we interpret and carry forward. If a site of memory belongs to everyone, how should it be understood, and whose voices should shape the way it is told? These are not abstract questions. They are the questions that every Egyptian student standing between those columns should feel encouraged to explore.
Source
"An original pedagogical listening script custom-authored by the curriculum development team; synthesized from the curatorial records of the Franco-Egyptian Centre for the Study of the Temples of Karnak (CFEETK), scaffolded to train auditory identification of prepositional phrases and model the JRE discursive framework."
JRE (Justify – Reason – Evidence) | مُجَادَبَ عِنْدَ إِجَابَةِ الكِتَاب.
1. Do you agree that Karnak represents continuity in Egyptian history? Give evidence for your answer. | SB
2. To what extent do the massive columns and hieroglyphics help communicate the power and beliefs of Ancient Egyptian civilization? | SB
3. Read the two views, then decide which one you agree with: | SB
- One view: Karnak is full of memories from the past. It was built and changed over about two thousand years, so the past is still there for us to see.
- The other view: Karnak is not only about the past. The writer asks: "Whose voices should shape its story?" A historical place stays "alive" when each new generation gives it a new meaning. Think about both views before you decide on your answer.

A) Answer the following questions:
1. Identify:
- Where is the speaker standing at the beginning of the recording? | SB
- Over how many years was Karnak Temple built? | SB
- What does the speaker find most significant? | SB
2. Explain: Why does the speaker contrast "silence" with "size" at the beginning of the recording? What effect does this create? | SB
3. Analyze: The speaker says Karnak is "a landscape of accumulated memory." What does this phrase mean? Give evidence from the recording. | SB
4. Evaluate: Why does the speaker say the Hypostyle Hall was designed "not simply to impress"? What was its real purpose? | SB

Definitions | التَّعْرِيفَات
accumulated | مُتَرَاكِم | built up or collected over time
devotion | إِخْلَاص | strong love and care for someone or something
encoded | مُشَفَّر | converted into signs or symbols to carry meaning
inscribed | مَنْقُوش | written or carved into a surface
massive | ضَخْم | extremely large in size
ram-headed sphinx | أَبُو الْهَوْل بِرَأْسِ كَبْش | an ancient Egyptian statue with a lion's body and a ram's head
representative | مَمِثَّل/مَنْدُوب | a person who speaks for others

◆ FOCUS on Vocabulary
لاحظ الفرق بين الكلمات التالية:
1 collect/gather
يجمع (يحضر أشياء بطريقة منظمة)
accumulate
يراكـم / يتراكم (يزيد تدريجيًا بمرور الوقت)
He collected/gathered information from several sources before writing his report.
She accumulated enough savings to buy her dream home.
2 road
طريق أي مسار بريدًا مكانين ( عام وشامل، ريف أو مدينة)
- The road between the two villages is very narrow.
- Be careful when crossing the road.
street
شارع (طريق داخل مدينة، تجاري به مياه من الجانبين، له أرصفة)
- Their shop is located on Main Street.
- The streets of Cairo are always busy.
avenue
طريق (واسع ومهم، غالبًا تصطف على جانبيه أشجار ومحلات أو مياه فاخرة)
- They walked along a beautiful avenue lined with trees.
- The company's headquarters is on Fifth Avenue in New York.
3 impressive
مبهر/ مؤثر (بوحص بالإعجاب)
The fireworks display was truly impressive and amazed the crowd.
affecting/moving
مثير للعاطفة / محرك للمشاعر
The sad movie had an affecting/moving impact on the audience.
effective
مؤثر (فعال ومفيد)
The new medicine proved to be effective in treating that مُعدٍ infectious disease.
4 landmark
معلم بارز (معنى مشهور) أو حدث تاريخي
- The Statue of Liberty is a famous landmark in New York.
- The discovery of penicillin was a landmark in medical history.
milestone
معلم هام / إنجاز كبير (حدث مهم يمثل مرحلة تحول أو تقدم في مسيرة شخص أو مشروع أو مجال معين)
The company reached a milestone when it sold its one-millionth product.

B Grammar Focus
Prepositional Phrases of Place
العبارات الظرفية الدالة على المكان
تعبّرنا العبارات الظرفية الدالة على المكان مكان وجود الشئ، أو أين يكون، أو أين يحدث. وهي أساسية في الكتابة التاريخية والوصفية.
أهم الحروف | الموقع النسبي | المجاورة والقرب | الموجة والوسط | الاتجاه | الاحتواء والحدود | الانطلاق والمدى
at | under | next to | in front of | across | inside | from ... to ...
in | below | beside | behind | along | outside |
on | over | by | between | through | beyond |
 | above | near/close to | among | around | |
 | | | opposite | | |
1 The most important prepositions of place أهم الحروف المتعلقة بالمكان
at | عند نقطة محددة – مع العناوين الصغيرة (شارع – حي) | at the entrance/at the top of the hill
in | للمدن والبلاد – داخل مساحة محاطة | in the bottle/in the classroom/in Luxor
on | فوق سطح مباشرة (ملامسة) أفقى أو رأسي | on the wall/on the Nile/on the screen
ملحوظة: تستخدم on للملامسة حتى ولو كان من أسفل فمثلاً:
The fly is on the ceiling.
الذبابة على السقف وهي تقع عليه من أسفل.
2 Relative Position الموقع النسبي
over | فوق / يمر بمحاذاة أعلى – تغطية شيء بالكامل | A plane flew over the city.
above | أعلى من / في مستوى أعلى وليس فوقه مباشرة | The temple stands above the river.
under | تحت / أسفل مباشرة ومغطى | The cat is under the table.
below | أدنى من / في مستوى أقل وليس تحته مباشرة | The valley is below the mountain.
3 Proximity المجاورة والقرب
next to/beside/by | بجانب تمامًا (لامس) | - Sit next to me.
 | | - There is a café by the station.
near/close to | بالقرب من (مسافة قصيرة) | near the metro station
4 Orientation الموجة والوسط
between | بين (أشياء أو أشخاص محددين ومفصلين، حتى لو كانوا أكثر من اثنين) | between Africa and Asia
among | بين (وسط مجموعة أو داخل مجموعة غير محددة) | among the ruins
in front of | أمام | in front of the temple
behind | خلف | behind the house
opposite | في الموجة (مجّها لوجه) | opposite the hotel

5 Spatial Extension الامتداد المكاني
across عبر/على الجانب الآخر | across the Nile Valley
along على طول (بمحاذاة خط) | along the banks of the Nile
through من خلال (عبرمجسم ثلاثي) | through the gate
around حول (يحيط بالمركز) | around the ancient city

6 Containment & Beyond الاحتواء والحدود
inside بالداخل تماما | inside the pyramid
outside بالخارج | outside the gate
beyond ما وراء (خلف الحدود) | beyond the desert lies the sea

7 Movement & Range الانطلاق والمدى
from ... to ... من ....إلى ....للتعبيرعن بداية ونهاية حركة أوامتداد | from Cairo to Luxor
towards تجاه | towards the river

◆ Topic overview | نظرة عامة على الموضوع
In what ways does a museum act as a "storyteller" rather than just a collection of old objects?
A museum is a storyteller because it does not just show us history; it interprets the past.
By choosing which artifacts to display and how to describe them, curation creates a narrative.
Inquiry Question: | سؤال بحثي
What does the word "curation" mean? How might it apply to history and museums?
ما معنى كلمة «curation»؟ وكيف يمكن تطبيقها على التاريخ والمتاحف؟
Suggested answer:
"Curation" comes from the Latin word "curare", meaning "to take care of." It refers to the act of selecting, organizing, caring for, and presenting a collection of items. A curator is the person responsible for this process. Curators decide which artifacts, documents, or artworks are displayed in museums and which remain in storage. This choice shapes what the public learns about the past.

◆ Reading Text | اقرأ القطعة ثم أجب عن الأسئلة الناضييج على أسئلة قطعة الفهم.
A Journey Through Time (Article)
Since the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM) opened its doors to the public on 4 November 2025, it has been described as the largest archaeological museum in the world. Located near the famous Pyramids of Giza, the museum covers 45,000 square meters and houses more than 100,000 artifacts(1) from Ancient Egypt. Among these treasures is the complete collection of Tutankhamun, displayed together for the first time in history. The impressive Grand Staircase alone features 87 colossal royal statues, arranged in chronological(2) order, offering visitors a breathtaking introduction to thousands of years of Egyptian civilization. Even though the museum is modern, it presents the story of one of the world's oldest civilizations.
Designing a museum of this scale is no simple task. Curators(3) must make careful decisions about which objects to display, how to arrange them, and what stories to tell. At the GEM, the journey begins in prehistory and moves forward through the great dynasties(4) of Ancient Egypt. This structure helps visitors understand how one of the world's greatest civilizations developed step-by-step over time. Multilingual(5) labels, interactive screens, and guided tours make the experience enjoyable and accessible(6) to Egyptian and international visitors of all ages.
One of the most exciting aspects of the GEM is its strong focus on education. School trips, workshops, and special programs are available to students across Egypt, giving young people the opportunity to connect with their heritage in a hands-on and memorable way. Although a single museum cannot include every story from Egypt's rich past, the GEM makes a remarkable effort to represent the depth and variety of Ancient Egyptian life—from royal tombs and temple art to everyday objects used by ordinary people thousands of years ago. Unlike many museums that are mainly designed for tourists, the GEM plays an important educational role for Egyptian students.
The GEM is not only a place to view ancient objects; it is also a space where science and history come together. Conservation(7) laboratories inside the museum allow experts to study and restore artifacts using the latest technology, ensuring that these national treasures are carefully preserved for future generations. The collection continues to grow, develop, and surprise its visitors, keeping the museum a dynamic experience for many years to come. Having successfully opened its doors to the public, the museum has firmly established itself as an important cultural landmark.
(1) القطع الأثرية | (2) ذو ترتيب زمني
(3) أمناء المتاحف | (4) السلالات الحاكمة
(5) متعدد اللغات | (6) متاح
(7) حفاظ/وقاية

"Synthesized and adapted by the curriculum development team from official Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM) press specifications, curatorial briefs, and heritage education frameworks such as UNESCO's World Heritage Education Programme."

B Grammar Focus

Prepositional Phrases of Time
العبارات الظرفية الدالة على الزمن
تُخبرنا العبارات الظرفية الدالة على الزمن بمتى حدث الشء أو كم استغرق من الوقت. وهي أساسية لتحديد التتابع الزمنى والمدة فى الكتابة التاريخية.

أهم الحروف | التتابع والبداية | الاحتوائية والحدود | الاتلاق والمدى
at/in/on | before/after/since | for/during/during/throughout | from ... to .../till/until/by/within

1 أهم الحروف المتعلقة بالوقت — The most important prepositions of time
at تُستخدم مع الساعات، الوجبات، العطلات الرسمية، واللحظات المحددة بدقة.
▸ at 9 a.m./at 5 p.m./at night/at noon/at midnight/at Eid/at Christmas
on تُستخدم مع أيام الأسبوع، التواريخ الكاملة (التى تحتوى على يوم)، وأيام المناسبات الخاصة.
▸ on Sunday/on Friday/on the 14th of October/on my birthday/on a warm summer day
in تُستخدم مع فترات اليوم (الصباح/المساء)، الشهور، الفصول، السنوات، القرون، والعصورالتاريخية.
▸ in the morning/in the afternoon/in October/in June/in winter/in summer/in 2026/in the 21st century

2 التتابع وبداية الوقت — Sequence & the Beginning of Time
before (قبل)
حدث يسبق وَقْتًا أو حدثًا آخر
▸ Wash your hands before dinner.
after (بعد)
حدث يقع تاليًا لوقت أو حدث آخر
▸ The tourists left after the sunset.
since (منذ – نقطة بداية الحدث)
تُحدد «نقطة انطلاق» الحدث فى الماضى (غالبًا مع زمن المضارع التام)، والحدث مستمر حتى الآن.
▸ The temple has stood here since 1300 BC.

الحَـذَر
إذا جاء اسم noun أو v. + ing بعد الكلمات الثلاث السابقة تعتبرها حروف جر، أما إذا جاءت بعدها جملة كاملة فتكون أدوات ربط linking words أو conjunctions مثال:
▸ After I had written the essay, I showed it to my teacher.
▸ Before I bought the car, I had saved enough money.
▸ Since the season started, we haven't lost a match.

3 مدة واستمرار الحدث — Duration & Time Periods
for (لمدة – مقدارالوقت)
تُستخدم لبيان «طول المدة الزمنية» أو المُستَقَرَّة (عدد الساعات، الأيام، السنين).
▸ for more than two thousand years
during (خلال /أثناء + اسم قِترة)
لبيان وقوع حدث ما فى وسط أو خلال فترة زمنية معلومة أو عهد معين (يُأتى بعدها اسم وليس مدة رَقَمية).
▸ During the reign of Ramesses II/during the match/during the night
throughout (على مدار/طوال)
تفيد الاستمرارية الشاملة من بداية الفترة إلى نهايتها دون انقطاع.
▸ It rained throughout the night.
since/for/during
since : بعدها «اسم» نقطة البداية (مثال: منذ عام ٦٠٠).
for : بعدها «مجموع» المدة الزمنية كمدد (مثال: لمدة ٦ سنوات).
during : بعدها «اسم الفترة» أو الحدث نفسه الذى وقع خِلاله الشئ (مثال: أثناء الحصبة، أثناء حكم الملك).

4 Deadlines & Time Ranges العددي الزمني والمواعيد النهائية
from ... to .../from ... until ...
(من... إلى...)
لتحدید العددي الزمني الكامل (نقطة البداية ونقطة النهاية لفترة ما)
from the 12th century to the present day
by
(بحلول / قبل وقت كنا كحد أقصى)
هنا بمعنى "في هذا الوقت أو قبله، وليس بعده".
You must finish the exam by 12 o'clock.
until/till
(حتى / إلى أن)
استمرار حالة معينة حتى نقطة زمنية محددة تتوقف عندها هذه الحالة.
The museum is open until 7 p.m.
حتى السابعة بعدها يغلق.
within
(في غضون / خلال مدة لا تتجاوز).
تضع حداً زمنياً يجب أن ينتهي الحدث قبله.
The project will be completed within three months.

1 Choose the correct answer from a, b, c, or d:
1. ......................... starting the lesson, the teacher had prepared the final revision booklet.
a) After b) Since c) For d) Before

a) in b) on c) since d) at
3. The student hasn't missed a single English grammar lecture ......................... the beginning of the second term.
a) at b) during c) since d) for
4. The final revision guide for the second secondary grade will be available ......................... exactly 4:00 p.m. tomorrow.
a) at b) during c) since d) for

a) After we finished the English exam, we felt relieved.
b) We had a short break after the English exam.
c) After he had studied the grammar rules, he answered the quiz.
d) They arrived at the museum after the bus had left.

(during) 6 a.m. and arrived at her home (3)......................... (on) about three hours. We spent the whole weekend there and returned (4)......................... (at) Sunday evening.

◆ Vocabulary Checkpoint 1
Choose the correct answer from a, b, c, or d:
1. The archaeologist's .................. that she had found a new pharaoh's tomb excited the whole world.
a) comfort | b) intention | c) claim | d) invitation
2. To meet the deadline, the team had to .................. the most important tasks first.
a) ignore | b) detect | c) innovate | d) prioritize
3. Before we post your review online, we must .................. that you actually bought the product from our store.
a) verify | b) hide | c) paint | d) arrange
4. The manager asked the team to .................. all the sales data from the past year before making a decision.
a) realize | b) analyze | c) forget | d) guess
5. The coach's inspiring speech helped .................. the players to give their best during the final match.
a) discourage | b) damage | c) motivate | d) innovate
6. Africa is the second-largest .................. in the world by both area and population.
a) island | b) country | c) planet | d) continent
7. Social media can quickly turn a simple idea into a worldwide .................. that can affect people everywhere.
a) trend | b) monument | c) current | d) joke
8. The witness did not .................. the details of the accident and reported exactly what happened.
a) contain | b) exaggerate | c) admire | d) appear

◆ Topic overview | نظرة عامة على الموضوع

What it means for historical content to "go viral"
To "go viral" means to spread rapidly and widely online (often within 24 hours). This spread is driven by emotional engagement (surprise, pride, or nostalgia) rather than historical accuracy or truth.

Inquiry Question: | سؤال بحثي

How can a historical event go viral? Give an example.
كيف يمكن لحدث تاريخي أن ينتشر على نطاق واسع؟ اذكر مثالاً.

Suggested answer:

A historical event goes viral when it spreads through media, education, art, and conversation—capturing the emotions and imagination of a large audience. For example, in 2019, Egypt moved a 3,000-year-old, 83-ton statue of Ramses II to the entrance of the Grand Egyptian Museum. The 12-hour operation was live-streamed and shared widely.

◆ Reading Text
اقرأ القطعة ثم أجب عن الأسئلة للتنويري على أسل قطعة الفهم.

The Algorithm and the Archive

Why Viral History Is Not Always True History
Never before in human history have historical images, artifacts, and claims(1) reached many people so quickly. A single post about an Egyptian pharaoh can accumulate millions of views within twenty-four hours; a colorized photograph of ancient Alexandria can be shared across continents before a single historian has had the opportunity to verify(2) its accuracy. The scale and speed of this spread are, in themselves, remarkable. The problem is that scale and speed have no real relationship to truth.
(1) يَتحقّق | (2) الادّعاءات
(3) يُحدد الأولويات | (4) باستمرار
(5) التثقيف الإعلامي

The way social media platforms work increases this risk considerably. These platforms are designed not to prioritize(3) accuracy but to promote engagement. Research consistently(4) shows that engagement is driven by emotion. Content that causes surprise, pride, nostalgia, or strong reaction spreads more rapidly than content that is measured, detailed, or carefully qualified. A viral post may claim that the Great Pyramid was built in a single decade by a team of fifty engineers. Such posts often accumulate more shares than carefully sourced corrections. In reality, the actual construction process unfolded over decades and involved tens of thousands of workers.

The consequences for our understanding of history are significant. In Egypt, where the relationship between ancient heritage and national identity is particularly important, the viral spread of historical myths and false claims risks distorting the public's understanding of who they are and where they come from.

Rarely do virality and accuracy move in the same direction. Only through deliberate media literacy(5) — the developed habit of questioning sources, checking dates, and consulting multiple perspectives — can citizens distinguish between the past that actually happened and the past that merely trends.

Source
Synthesized and adapted by the national curriculum development team from contemporary digital humanities literature, algorithmic engagement studies, and media literacy frameworks, contextualized with historical case studies of Egyptian heritage.

◆ FOCUS on Vocabulary

لاحظ الفرق بين الكلمات التالية:

(1) advocate | يدعو إلى/يناصر (بشكل علني ونشط).
- The organization advocates for stricter environmental laws.
- He advocates reducing the working week to four days.
recommend | يوصي/يقترح
The doctor recommended getting at least eight hours of sleep.
endorse | يؤيد/يبارك رسميًا (غالبًا للتجارة أو السياسة).
- The famous athlete endorsed a new sports drink in a TV commercial.
- The former president endorsed the young candidate for senator.

(2) image | الصورة الذهنية/الانطباع العام.
The company is trying to improve its image by using eco-friendly packaging.
reputation | السمعة /ما يشتهربه الشخص.
- This restaurant has a great reputation for serving fresh seafood.
stereotype | الصورة النمطية /القالب النمطي.
- It is unfair to judge someone based on the stereotype that all teenagers are lazy.

(3) legend | أسطورة (قصصة تعتمد على حقائق مع المبالغة فيها).
Abu Zaid El Hilaly is one of the most famous Arab legends.
myth | أسطورة (قصصة لا تعتمد على حقائق).
It's a complete myth that eating carrots helps you to see in the dark.
fable | قصصة أسطورية (قصصة عن الحيوانات أو الطبيعة لتوصيل عبرة).
The Rabbit and the Tortoise is an old fable that is known in many cultures.

(4) habit | عادة (فردية).
Brushing your teeth every morning is a good habit.
custom | عرف/عادة اجتماعية.
It is a local custom to greet guests with tea.
tradition | تقليد (متوارث).
Celebrating New Year is a family tradition.

B Grammar Focus
Concession Clauses
عبارات الاستدراك
عندما يبين الشخص اعتراضه على شيء فإنه يستخدم عبارات مهمة تبيّن ذلك وهذا يظهر عند كتابة الموضوعات الجدلية (argumentative) وهو قاعدة أساسية في اللغة الإنجليزية تأتي عليها أسئلة متعددة في جزء القواعد ومن هذه العبارات:

Form | Meaning | Examples
Although + clause | بالرغم من أن | Although it was raining, we went for a walk.
Even though + clause | على الرغم من أن | Even though he studied hard, he didn't get a full mark.
Despite + noun phrase | على الرغم من+جملة اسمية | Despite the cold weather, she wore a T-shirt.
In spite of + noun/v-ing | على الرغم من (مثل Despite) | In spite of being tired, he finished his homework.
While it is true that ... | في حين أنه صحيح أن | While it is true that money is important, it cannot buy happiness.
Admittedly ... | حقيقةً ....../الاعتراف بالحق | Admittedly, the exam was difficult; however, everyone passed.
Nevertheless ... | ومع ذلك/بالرغم من ذلك بعد الفاصلة المنقوطة | She was very afraid; nevertheless, she entered the dark room.
It may be argued that ... | قد يُجادل البعض بأن | It may be argued that online learning is easier; nevertheless, classrooms are better.
however,... | ومع ذلك/لكن/مهما يكون | The food was expensive; however, it was delicious.
but | لكن | He is rich, but he is not happy.
On the other hand, ... | من ناحية أخرى | Living in cities is exciting. On the other hand, it is very noisy.
Whereas + clause | في حين أن/بينما | My brother likes sports, whereas I prefer reading.
Whatever + noun/noun + subj. + verb | مهما/على الرغم من | - Whatever his mistakes, I will forgive him. - Whatever mistakes he makes, I will forgive him.

هناك بعض العبارات والكلمات يجب أن يتماوف عليها الطلاب ليسهل عليه الفهم في كثيرمن القواعد ومنها:
Clause | هي الجملة الكاملة التي تحتوي على فاعل وفعل.
Phrase | هي الجملة التي ليست بها فعل ولكن بها (اسم أو v.ing).

ملاحظات علي بعض الروابط

1 While it is true that/It may be argued that

1 While it is true that .................... . | في حين أنه صحيح (أومسلّم به) ...
عندما نسلم بحقيقة واضحة في البداية ثم نذكر الجانب الآخر.
► While it is true that fast food is delicious, it is very unhealthy.

2 It may be argued that .................... . | يمكن أن يجادل البعض بأن
عند طرح وجهة نظر قابلة للنقاش وليست حقيقة مطلقة وغالباً نرد عليها بعد ذلك بجملة مثل but أو لكي نقول رأينا.
► It may be argued that exams are unfair, but they are necessary to test skills.

2 Admittedly
معناها «بالاعتراف الجماع»، «في الحقيقة»، «بلا شك»، وهي ظرف وتأتي في أول الجملة وبعدها comma في المنتصف but أو however ويمكن أن تأتي في منتصف الجملة أيضًا.
Admittedly, I made a mistake, but I'm trying to fix it.
The movie was admittedly slow at the beginning, but the ending was amazing.
Extra Points | نقاط إضافية
However + adj. + subj. + verb, جملة | مهما يكون | However ill he was, he went to school.
جملة + However, + . جملة | ولكن | He was ill. However, he went to school.
جملة + ; however, + جملة | ولكن | He was ill; however, he went to school.
جملة +, but/yet + جملة | ولكن | He was ill, but/yet he went to school.
Whatever + clause | مهما | Whatever you do, I won't punish you.
Whatever + verb | مهما/أيًا ما | Whatever happens, stay calm.
Although أول الجملة أو منتصفها | بالرغم من أن | - Although he is rich, he isn't happy. - He isn't happy although he is rich.
Despite أول الجملة أو منتصفها | على الرغم من | - Despite his height, he couldn't hang the picture. - He couldn't hang the picture despite his height.
جملة +, while + جملة | بينما | I love drinking coffee, while my brother prefers tea.

◆ Topic overview | نظرة عامة على الموضوع

What does it mean to document historical events?
To document a historical event means to create a lasting record of an occurrence through primary evidence—such as text, photographs, or video—that can be analyzed and verified by future generations. Traditionally, this was the job of "official" gatekeepers like government ministries, academic historians, or professional news outlets.

Inquiry Question: | سؤال بحثي
What is 'citizen journalism'? How has social media changed the way historical events are documented?
ما المقصود ب «صحافة المواطن»؟ وكيف غيّرت وسائل التواصل الاجتماعي طريقة توثيق الأحداث التاريخية؟

Suggested answer:
Citizen journalism is when ordinary people collect, document, and share news and information, usually through smartphones and social media platforms. Social media has made historical documentation instant, diverse, permanent, and global—giving everyone a voice in writing history.

◆ Listening Text
Scan & listen

"How social media is bringing Egyptian discoveries to the world"
For most of human history, news of a great archaeological discovery travels slowly. A royal tomb found in the Valley of the Kings might be reported in a specialist journal months after the excavation(1) began, reaching only a small community of scholars and museum professionals. The wider public, whether in Egypt or abroad, would wait years before seeing even a photograph of what had been uncovered. Knowledge of the past was carefully managed, moving through official channels before it reached ordinary people.
Social media has transformed this process in remarkable(2) ways. When an exciting find is made today—whether a sealed tomb in Luxor, a submerged(3) city off the coast of Alexandria, or an ancient papyrus in the Delta—it can be photographed, posted, and shared with millions of people within hours. Official accounts run by organizations such as the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities now use platforms like X and Instagram to document discoveries in real time, allowing followers from Cairo to Tokyo to watch history being uncovered. For the first time, Egypt's extraordinary heritage is being shared with the world at the very moment it is found.
There are challenges to consider, however. A post on X can be deleted, an Instagram story expires after 24 hours, and a TikTok video may be removed by its creator or by the platform's moderation systems within minutes of going viral. Unlike a stone inscription or a printed journal, social media documentation(4) is fragile(5). There is also the question of accuracy(6): not every post about an Egyptian discovery is published by experts, and images or claims can sometimes be misunderstood or shared out of context.
Specialists argue that social media is most valuable when it works alongside careful academic documentation and preservation.

مميز / رائع / حديث بالملابسحنية (2) | أعمال حفر / التنقيب (1)
تنظيم بالمستندات (4) | مفهوم تحت الماء (3)
دقة (6) | هش / قابل للكسر (5)

Definitions    التعريفات

excavation | حفر/تنقيب | the activity of digging to discover old objects or buildings
remarkable | مميز/رائع | very unusual or surprising in a positive way
submerged | مغمور | covered or hidden under water
documentation | توثيق | the process of recording and keeping information, evidence, or details
fragile | هش/قابل للكسر | easily damaged or broken
accuracy | دقة | the state of being correct and free from mistakes
citizen journalism | صحافة المواطنين | news reporting carried out by members of the public, not trained journalists
real-time documentation | توثيق فوري | recording and sharing events as they happen, without delay
hashtag | هاشتاج | a word or phrase preceded by # used on social media to tag content by topic
digital archive | أرشيف رقمي | a collection of historical materials stored and accessible online
selective framing | التأطير الانتقائي | choosing which details to include or exclude to shape the audience's understanding

◆ FOCUS on Vocabulary

احظر الفرق بين الكلمات التالية:

1 dig    يحفر/ينبش (عام، بيدوى غالبًا).
- The dog dug a hole in the garden.
- We need to dig a small trench مجرى for the drainage pipe.

excavate    يحفر/ينقب (بشكل منهجي وعلمي، غالبًا لأغراض أثرية أو انشائية كبيرة).
- Archaeologists excavated the Ancient Roman Temple.
- Workers excavated the site before building the skyscraper.

drill (bore)    يحفر/يثقب (بألة دوارة، غالبًا لعمل ثقب عميق أو ضيق بجدا عن شيء، أو لعمل شيء).
- The crew drilled 200 meters into the ground to find water.
- He drilled a hole in the wall to hang a picture.
- They plan to bore a tunnel through the mountain.

2 delay    يؤخر/يؤجل (سبب خارجي أو داخلي، قد يكون اضطراريًا).
- The flight was delayed due to heavy rain.
- Please don't delay sending the report.
- She delayed her trip until next week.

procrastinate    يماطل/يسوف/يؤجل (بسبب كسل أو خوف أو عدم رغبة).
- Stop procrastinating and start your homework!
- He procrastinated for weeks instead of applying for the job.
- I always procrastinate when the task is boring.

3 statement    بيان/تصريح (قصيد، رسمي غالبًا، شخصي أو مكتوب)
- The CEO released a statement about the new company policy.
- The witness gave a statement to the police.

speech    خطاب/كلمة (طويل، شخصي، أمام جمهور، غالبًا عاطفي أو تحفيزي)
- The president delivered a powerful speech about unity.
- She gave a heartfelt speech at her best friend's wedding.

presentation    عرض تقديمي (منظم، مع وسائل مساعدة مثل شرائح، بهدف شرح أو إيع فكرة)
- He gave a presentation on climate change using detailed slides.
- The sales team prepared a presentation for their new product.

Prepositions of time
Preposition | Meaning | Example
at | - في (الوقت المحدد) - تُستخدم مع الساعات، الويجات، العطلات الرسمية، واللحظات المحددة بدقة. | - at 9 a.m./at 5 p.m. - at night/at noon/at midnight - at Eid/at Christmas
on | - في (اليوم /التاريخ) - تُستخدم مع أيام الأسبوع، التواريخ الكاملة (التي تحتوي على يوم)، وأيام المناسبات الخاصة. | - on Sunday/on Friday - on the 14th of October - on my birthday/on a warm summer day
in | - في (للفترات الطويلة) - تُستخدم مع فترات اليوم (الصباح /المساء)، الشهور، الفصول، السنوات، القرون، والعصور التاريخية. | - in the morning/in the afternoon/ - in October/in June - in winter/in summer - in 2026/in the 21st century
before | - قبل -حدث يسبق وقتًا أو حدثًا آخر. | - Wash your hands before dinner.
after | - بعد -حدث يقع تاليًا لوقت أو حدث آخر. | - The tourists left after the sunset.
since | - منذ (نقطة البداية) - تحدد نقطة انطلاق الحدث في الماضي (غالبًا مع زمن المضارع التام)، والحدث مستمر حتى الآن. | - The temple has stood here since 1300 BC.
for | - لمدة (مقدارالوقت) - تُستخدم لبيان طول المدة الزمنية المستغرفة (عدد الساعات، الأيام، السنين). | - I've studied English for 11 years.
during | - خلال /أثناء (+ اسم) - لبيان وقوع حدث ما في وسط أو خلال فترة زمنية معلومة أو عهدة معين (يأتي بعدها اسم وليس مدة رقمية). | - During the reign of Ramesses II, Egypt built some of its most extraordinary temples.
throughout | - على مدار /طوال - تقيد الاستمرارية الشاملة من بداية الفترة إلى نهايتها دون انقطاع. | - It rained throughout the night.
from ... to ... | -من...إلى... - لتحديد المدي الزمني الكامل (نقطة البداية ونقطة النهاية لفترة ما). | - The library is open from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
by | - بحلول /قبل وقت كذا - تقيد معنى في هذاالوقت أو قبله، وليس بعده (حد أقصى). | - You must finish the exam by 12 o'clock.
until | - حتى /إلى أن - استمرار حالة معينة حتى نقطة زمنية محددة تتوقف عندها هذه الحالة. | - The museum is open until 7 p.m.

الفرق بين حرف الجر وأداة الربط:
- إذا جاء اسم أو v-ing بعد (After/Before/Since) تُعتبارحرف جرا (Preposition)
- أما إذا جاءت بعدها جملة كاملة (فاعل + فعل) تكون أدوات ربط (Conjunctions/Linking words).
Preposition | Conjunction/Linking word
Check your answers before submitting the exam. | After I had written the essay, I showed it to my teacher.
The tourists left after sunset. | Before I bought the car, I had saved enough money.
After finishing my homework, I went to sleep. | Since the season started, we haven't lost a match.
He has lived here since 2015/since last Monday. |
She has been famous since her first movie. |
Concession Clauses | عبارات الاستدراك
الروابط المتبوعة بجملة كاملة Clause: فاعل + فعل:
Although/though | بالرغم من أن | Although he was tired, he continued working.
Even though | مع أن | Even though he studied hard, he didn't pass.
While it is true that ... | في حين أنه صحيح أن | While it is true that money is important, it cannot buy happiness.
It may be argued that ... | قد يجادل البعض بأن | It may be argued that homework is unnecessary, but it improves learning
الروابط المتبوعة يـشبه جملة (Phrase). اسم/ v-ing /ضمير
Despite | على الرغم من | Despite the rain, we went out. Despite being ill, he passed the exams.
In spite of | | In spite of being tired, he finished his work. In spite of feeling exhausted, Sarah stayed up late to finish her report.
روابط الظروف وحالات خاصة (Adverbs & Special Structures)
Admittedly | باعتراف الجميع/ حقًا | Admittedly, the exam was difficult, but everyone passed.
However, | لكن /مهما/مع ذلك /غيرأن | He was tired. However, he continued working. He was tired; however, he continued working. However difficult the exam was, he succeeded.
but/yet | لكن /ومع ذلك | He is rich, but/yet he isn't happy.
whereas/while | بينما/في حين أن | Ali likes football, whereas/while his brother prefers tennis.
On the other hand | من ناحية أخرى | City life is exciting. On the other hand, it is crowded.
Whatever | مهما | Whatever you do, I will support you. Whatever his mistakes, I forgave him.

القسم C | Section (C): المهارات — Study Skills

Dicsursive Essay | المقال الجدلي
A discursive essay is a form of writing that examines an issue from multiple perspectives.
المقال الجدلي هو شكل من أشكال الكتابة التي تتناول قضية ما من وجهات نظر متعددة.
Types Of Discursive Essays
Opinion-Based Discursive Essay | For and Against Essay | Solution-Oriented Essay
مقال جدلي قائم على الرأي | مقال مؤيد ومعارض | مقال موجه نحو الحلول
You share your opinion, but you also consider both sides of the issue. After fairly discussing the different viewpoints, you clearly explain your opinion.
تُبدى رأيك، لكنك تراعي أيضاً وجهتي النظر في القضية. وبعد مناقشة وجهات النظر المختلفة بموضوعية، توضح رأيك بوضوح.
You discuss the advantages and disadvantages of a topic equally, without supporting one side more than the other.
تناكش مزايا وعيوب الموضوع بالتساوي، دون تفضل جانب على آخر.
You introduce a problem and explore various solutions—from different perspectives.
تقوم بطرح مشكلة واستكشاف حلول متنوعة - من وجهات نظر مختلفة.
Structure of Discursive Essays
Introduce the topic clearly.
قدم الموضوع بوضوح.
Give background information to help readers understand the context.
قدم معلومات أساسية لمساعدة القراء على فهم السياق.
End with a thesis statement that outlines what the passage will discuss.
اختم ببيان أطروحة يحدد ما سيناقشه النص.
2 Body 1
Present the first point in favor of the topic with supporting examples.
اعرض النقطة الأولى المؤيدة للموضوع مع تقديم أمثلة داعمة.
3 Body 2
Present the opposing point with reasons.
اعرض وجهة النظر المعارضة مع ذكر الأسباب.
4 Conclusion
Summarize all arguments and provide a reasoned conclusion. Avoid introducing new points in this section.
لخص جميع الحجج وقدم استنتاجاً منطقياً. تجنب إدخال نقاط جديدة في هذا القسم.

MODEL Discursive ESSAY
Social media has done more harm than good to our understanding of Egyptian history. Discuss.
Introduction | Social media makes learning about ancient Egypt accessible and engaging for everyone. However, it also spreads a lot of false information very quickly across the internet. Many viral videos share rumors instead of verified facts. Overall, social media does more harm than good because it values likes and views over real history.
Body 1 | The biggest problem is that online computer algorithms love shocking stories. Because of this, viral videos often claim that aliens built the Pyramids or that mummies carry magical curses. These fake stories get millions of views, while real discoveries by actual experts get completely ignored. This misleads both students and adults, encouraging them to accept baseless myths instead of learning true history.
Body 2 | On the other hand, the internet significantly aids in public appreciation for the ancient world. Great museums and local Egyptian scientists can share new discoveries instantly on mobile devices. This makes history exciting for young people who cannot travel to see the monuments in person. It also lets modern Egyptians tell their own stories and protect their own rich cultural heritage.
Conclusion | In the end, social media brings people closer to Egypt's past but mixes too much fiction with fact. The constant flood of historical misinformation makes it hard for anyone to find the truth online. Until we learn to look at videos with a critical eye, the internet will keep hiding real achievements. We must protect true history from being lost behind a big wall of internet-tricky stories made just for views!
تحدي
والنتيجة كان تفوق كل المتددينات

1 Read the following passage, then answer the questions:

History is not just a collection of old stories; it is a living connection between the past and the present. Every society has historical sites, monuments, and museums that preserve memories of important events and people. These places help us understand how previous generations lived, worked, and faced challenges. When people visit a museum, they do
(5) more than look at old objects. They discover stories that explain the development of their communities and nations. In this way, museums act as storytellers, keeping history alive for future generations.
Today, technology has changed the way people interact with history. Through social media, websites, and digital archives, historical information can reach millions of people
(10) in a very short time. Photos, videos, and personal accounts of historical events can be shared worldwide, encouraging people to learn more about their heritage. For example, old photographs uploaded online may help young people visualize events that happened decades ago. As a result, history has become more accessible than ever before.
However, the digital age also presents challenges. Not everything shared online is accurate.
(15) Some information may be misleading, incomplete, or even false. Therefore, historians, teachers, and researchers must carefully verify facts before presenting them to the public. Reliable sources remain essential for understanding the past correctly.
By combining traditional methods of preservation with modern technology, societies can protect their cultural heritage while making it relevant to today's world. Understanding
(20) history helps people appreciate their identity, learn valuable lessons, and avoid repeating mistakes. Although the past cannot be changed, its echoes continue to influence our decisions, shape our values, and guide us toward a better future.
